coordinates.locator: geometry:chooz-far-laboratory (two-circle intersection of the TDR baselines about the B1/B2 unit centroids)
coordinates.note: Derived, not published: the far laboratory is placed where the Double Chooz baselines (1114.6 m and 997.9 m) meet, choosing the solution under the hill near Chooz A. If the TDR's RE/RW labels were geographic the point would move ~1.6 km; see the geometry record and docs/atlas-worklog/RELEASE_GEOMETRY_underground.md.

depth_mwe.note: Sourced from Wikipedia (rank 12) only this session.
depth_mwe.quote: 300 meters of water equivalent of shielding from cosmic muons

name: Double Chooz far detector site
notes: The Double Chooz far detector was placed inside a hill (former site of the CHOOZ experiment's own far detector) at 1050 m from the reactor cores, per the 2012 discovery paper's abstract.

summary.plain: A hall inside a hill near the Chooz nuclear plant in France, over a kilometre from the reactors, shielded by rock from cosmic rays.
summary.technical: Double Chooz far-detector hall, 1050 m from the Chooz-B reactor cores, under ~300 m.w.e. of rock shielding.
